extracted.intended_audience: Cochrane review authors and medical/healthcare librarians / information specialists involved in systematic reviews of interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Planning, designing, running, documenting and implementing searches and study-selection processes to identify studies for Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions, in collaboration with information specialists. Covers choice of sources, search strategy design, minimizing bias, retrieving unpublished/ongoing data, and study-level selection and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the information specialist / librarian
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical/healthcare librarians and information specialists have an integral role in the production of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work closely with review authors from protocol stage; advise on which databases and other sources to search; design or provide guidance on search strategies; run searches where available; save and collate results and share in appropriate formats; draft or help draft search methods sections of protocols/reviews/updates; advise on searching sources beyond main bibliographic databases and how to download results; organize translations or data extraction from non-English reports; obtain copies of trial reports (within copyright); advise on and collaborate on reference management and review production tools (Covidence, EPPI-Reviewer, RevMan); check and format references per the Cochrane Style Manual; keep up to date with Cochrane methodological developments and, where applicable, maintain Specialized Registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing bias in the search process
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews require a thorough, objective and reproducible search of a range of sources to identify as many eligible studies as possible (within resource limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search beyond MEDLINE; avoid relying on a single database; be aware of publication bias and language bias when restricting searches; balance thoroughness with efficiency given time/budget constraints; searches should be motivated by eligibility criteria; peer review search strategies before running; consider the impact of restricted searches on bias and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studies (not reports) are the unit of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews have studies as the primary units of interest and analysis; a single study may have more than one report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search processes typically retrieve reports/records, so review teams must identify and associate multiple reports of the same study manually or via study-based sources; consider study-based registers that link records of the same study; use processes/software to select and group publications by study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and licensing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to copyright legislation and the terms of licensing agreements for databases and other resources when searching and obtaining records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow terms and conditions when searching databases and downloading records; adhere to copyright when obtaining copies of publications and other records; seek guidance from information specialists since legislation and licences vary by jurisdiction and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search bibliographic databases extensively (CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, together with Embase (if access is available), should be searched for all Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches may be done directly or via a CRG's Specialized Register; database selection should be guided by the topic; searching two or more databases lowers the risk of missing eligible studies; coverage and comprehensiveness vary by topic so consider additional databases for specialised or cross-disciplinary topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: MECIR C19: Planning the search (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance the methods to be used for identifying studies. Design searches to capture as many studies as possible that meet the eligibility criteria, ensuring that relevant time periods and sources are covered and not restricted by language or publication status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches should be motivated directly by the eligibility criteria for the review; if searches are restricted by publication status or language, this can introduce publication or language bias; restrictions should instead be applied in eligibility criteria where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: MECIR C24: Search CENTRAL, MEDLINE and Embase (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search the Cochrane Review Group’s Specialized Register (internally or via CENTRAL). Ensure that CENTRAL, MEDLINE and Embase (if available) have been searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the minimum databases for Cochrane intervention reviews; searching a CRG Specialized Register that is comprehensive and up to date may substitute for separate searches of CENTRAL, MEDLINE and Embase (with caveats); expertise may be needed to avoid duplication of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both free-text terms and controlled vocabulary / subject headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Both free-text and subject headings (e.g. MeSH and Emtree) should be used in search strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine text words and controlled vocabulary to maximise retrieval; verify controlled vocabulary terms and their scope across interfaces and over time; consider interface-specific indexing differences (PubMed, Ovid, Embase platforms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure search strategies: avoid too many different concepts; use OR within concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategies should avoid using too many different search concepts but a wide variety of search terms should be combined with OR within each included concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep concept structure simple to maximise sensitivity; use comprehensive term lists within each concept combined with OR, then combine concepts (e.g. population/intervention) to restrict results; too many concepts can reduce sensitivity and miss studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for high sensitivity (accept lower precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches should aim for high sensitivity, which may result in relatively low precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise identifying as many eligible studies as possible, accepting that more irrelevant records will be retrieved and screened; consider resources for screening workload and methods to manage large result sets (automation, machine classifiers, text mining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use published, validated search filters where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Published, highly sensitive, validated search filters to identify randomized trials should be considered, such as the Cochrane Highly Sensitive Search Strategies for identifying randomized trials in MEDLINE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider Cochrane filters for Embase and CINAHL where appropriate; weigh benefits of validated filters against the risk of excluding relevant records; verify filter performance for the review topic and interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not apply randomized trial and human filters to CENTRAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized trial and human filters are not required in CENTRAL and should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CENTRAL is already a highly sensitive collection of trial records; applying such filters may unnecessarily reduce retrieval of eligible records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: All search strategies should be peer reviewed, before being run, by a suitably qualified and experienced medical/healthcare librarian or information specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review improves quality and reproducibility; methods and evidence supporting peer review are described elsewhere in the Handbook and Technical Supplement; incorporate feedback and document peer review in the review methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Specialized Registers and use Cochrane Centralised Search Service where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where available, the Specialized Register(s) of the relevant Cochrane Group(s) should be searched for all Cochrane reviews, either internally within the Cochrane Group or via CENTRAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some CRGs maintain Specialized Registers which may allow a more precise search with fewer records to screen; consider time lags between databases and Registers and evaluate comprehensiveness before substituting direct database searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search appropriate national, regional and subject-specific databases (MECIR C25 Highly desirable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search appropriate national, regional and subject-specific bibliographic databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Databases relevant to the review topic should be covered (e.g. CINAHL for nursing, APA PsycInfo for psychological interventions); regional databases (e.g. LILACS) and country-specific databases should be considered to reduce language and regional publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search trials registers and trials results registers
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials registers should be searched for all Cochrane reviews and trials results registers are important for identifying study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP and other registries; registry records help identify ongoing and unpublished trials and may provide protocol and results information not in journals; consider registry-record duplicates and multiple registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search regulatory agency sources and clinical study reports (CSRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory agency sources and clinical study reports are increasingly important for identifying study results and detailed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSRs often provide more complete methods and results than journal publications or registry records; regulatory sources can change review conclusions in some cases; consider feasibility and access (FOIA, requests to manufacturers) and document efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify ongoing and unpublished studies; contact individuals and organisations (MECIR C31 Highly desirable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact relevant individuals and organisations for information about unpublished or ongoing studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact trial authors, experts, pharmaceutical companies, trial units; send lists of identified studies and eligibility criteria to elicit additional studies; use email, ResearchGate, LinkedIn or project websites; include characteristics of ongoing studies in 'Characteristics of ongoing studies' table; document contacts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting and reporting the search process (PRISMA / PRISMA-S / MECIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search methods and the search process should be documented and reported in line with MECIR expectations and current reporting guidance for PRISMA and PRISMA-S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document full strategies, dates, interfaces, limits applied, search results, and peer review; use flow diagrams for tracking records and screening; provide reproducible search documentation (Technical Supplement contains more detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and group multiple reports from the same study
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify multiple reports from the same study and associate them to the study-level unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use study-based sources and registers where possible; manually link multiple reports and extract complementary information from different reports; ensure correct counting of studies (not reports) in analyses and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical process for selecting studies and selecting 'excluded studies'
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a reproducible process for screening records and selecting studies for inclusion or exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear eligibility criteria; document reasons for exclusion and produce an 'Excluded studies' list/table; set out screening workflow (title/abstract followed by full-text), who screens (single vs double screening), and how disagreements are resolved; report implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software support for selecting studies and reference management
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reference management and review production tools to manage searches, screening and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider Covidence, EPPI-Reviewer, RevMan and other software; information specialists can save and collate results and share in appropriate formats; use deduplication, screening modules, and export formats to support reproducible workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of searches, alerts, and when to stop searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan timing of searches, set up alerts, and decide criteria for stopping searches and for updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider when to run searches relative to project timelines; set up alerts to capture new records during review production and for updates; use stopping criteria pragmatically (resource limits, diminishing returns) and document rationale for stopping and for update timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, date and document format restrictions: avoid in the search
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not restrict searches by language, date or document format in a way that could introduce bias; remove restrictions only via eligibility criteria if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing language restrictions in English-language databases is not a substitute for searching non-English journals and databases; organize translations or at minimum data extraction where required for non-English reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify fraudulent studies, retracted publications, errata and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategies should include approaches to identifying fraudulent studies, retracted publications, errata and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bibliographic databases, publishers' retraction notices, Retraction Watch, and link checking; consider implications for inclusion and sensitivity analyses if problematic reports are identified; document detection methods and actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance thoroughness and efficiency; consider automation and abbreviated searches carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Time and budget restraints require balancing thoroughness with efficiency; automation and abbreviated searches may be considered but have trade-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine classifiers, text mining and automation can reduce workload but require validation; abbreviated searches (e.g. MEDLINE+CENTRAL) may be acceptable for rapid evidence syntheses where decision-makers accept some risk; decisions demanding high certainty require comprehensive searches.
